name: US equity stress
summary: S&P 500 ended 6 Nov 5.7% below its high; VIX 25.6, inside the Watch band; US markets reopen on 9 Nov
state: The S&P 500 closed near 7,377 on 6 Nov, 5.7% below its 52-week high and 2.2% lower on the week, with a worst single day of −4.4% in the past five sessions (Yahoo Finance). The VIX closed at 25.6, up 21% on the week and below the 30 Alert line. No US session has closed since 6 Nov, so these remain the latest readings as of 9 Nov.
for_you: Pension and investment valuations tied to US shares move with these swings. Volatility at this level means larger daily moves in valuations than in calmer periods.
rubric_hit: VIX 23.4 ≥ 20 Watch line; S&P drawdown 5.65% ≥ 5% Watch line
why: The S&P 500 is the world's risk barometer; sharp falls and spiking volatility transmit to pensions, credit and confidence globally.
drivers: Earnings, interest-rate expectations, liquidity, geopolitical shocks, positioning and leverage.

rubric.alert: VIX > 30, or drawdown > 15%, or a market-wide circuit breaker trips.
rubric.normal: VIX < 20 and S&P 500 drawdown from 52-week high < 5%.
